chain_trace.break_detail: Two script-level breaks. (1) Wrong route: no /cluster/collection/{collection_name} route exists in qdrant v1.18.0 (absent from src/actix routing and from openapi/openapi-collections.ytt.yaml, which places collection cluster info at /collections/{collection_name}/cluster); every probe in this log — including all the 404s — hit a nonexistent route, so the endpoint under assertion was never exercised (corroborated: sibling scripts boundary_cluster_collection_info_001/002/004/005 all ended in SCRIPT_ERROR with 'existing collection answered 404 / assertion promises 200'). (2) Client-side input dissolution: raw-socket wire capture with the log-producing interpreter (requests 2.32.5, urllib3 2.6.3) shows /cluster/collection/.. is sent as 'GET /cluster/ HTTP/1.1'; actix NormalizePath::trim() (src/actix/mod.rs:121) strips the trailing slash and the request matches #[get("/cluster")] whose handler returns dispatcher.cluster_status() = ClusterStatus::Disabled on this single-node deployment (lib/storage/src/dispatcher.rs:264-269) — producing exactly the observed body {"result":{"status":"disabled"},"status":"ok","time":...}. The verdict's causal story ('never-creatable collection name answered 200 where the assertion documents 404') is therefore false: no collection-name lookup ever occurred.
